DISPLAY / EDITORIAL SERIF

From the ground up.

Body copy uses a clear system sans with comfortable line length and generous spacing. Hero service labels use Jura. The shared photo hero and circular mark appear across Home, Access, Form, Studio and Contact.

02Identity

The UIR logo

Three forms, one measured mark.

The U and lowercase r are each 100 × 100 units. The I is 20 × 200 units, twice their height. All three forms use a 20-unit stroke and the gaps between U–I and I–r are both 10 units. A 20-unit blue square sits at the top centre of the U; a 20-unit clay square aligns to the bottom-right corner of the r. Keep these proportions and alignments when scaling the mark. The circular hero treatment and service name are separate from the logo.

03Selected work

04Accessibility by default

Patterns are part of the practice.

Keyboard: every interactive element has a visible focus treatment, follows a logical tab order and remains operable without a pointer.

Structure: pages use landmarks, one main heading, meaningful section headings and accessible names for controls and images.

Motion: movement is restrained and reduced when a visitor prefers less motion; content never depends on hover alone.

Contrast: text meets 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text); essential control boundaries and focus indicators meet 3:1 on their adjacent colours.

Targets and reflow: controls have at least 24 × 24 CSS pixels of target area; content remains available at 320 CSS pixels and with increased text spacing.

Colour use: moss, sky and logo blue are accents rather than body-text colours unless a specific text/background pair is checked.

05Maintaining the system

Add with intention.

  1. Start with an existing token or component before introducing another.
  2. Keep names and code in the shared component module; update the documentation with the code.
  3. Check the pattern at mobile, tablet and desktop widths.
  4. Verify keyboard use, reduced motion, readable contrast and heading order whenever a pattern changes.
  5. Use confirmed project details and approved imagery only. Keep portfolio cards out until the work is ready to share.
